answer: Every agent holds a quill — a single signing key bound to its hardware, used to ink each completed job into a public ledger. A small trusted kernel re-runs one random job per epoch and checks the quill's signature against the ledger; a mismatch burns the stake. Reputation accrues like shale: each verified job lays down one thin layer, and layers only harden after a full epoch of honest work, so a swarm of fresh fakes has only dust where honest agents have solid rock.
